title: Prototype Chain Walker & Distance Calculator
problemStatement: Implement `getPrototypeDepth(obj)` that traverses an object's prototype chain and returns the number of hops until `null` is reached. If `obj` is null or undefined, return 0.
interviewTrap: Using `__proto__` directly is deprecated. Always prefer `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)`.

testCases.name: Standard object literal has depth of 1 (Object.prototype -> null)
Object created with Object.create(null) has depth 0
Inherited chain depth reflects hierarchy
testCases.testFn: const parent = {}; const child = Object.create(parent); return getPrototypeDepth(child);

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Every JS object has an internal `[[Prototype]]` link. Property lookup walks this chain until the property is found or `null` is reached (`Object.prototype.__proto__ === null`). Modifying a property on an instance creates an 'own property' shadowing the prototype's property.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for [[Prototype]] Traversal to Object.prototype and null.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), [[Prototype]] Traversal to Object.prototype and null is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Using `__proto__` directly is deprecated. Always prefer `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)`.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is the difference between __proto__ and prototype?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `prototype` is a property found exclusively on constructor functions (and classes); it defines the object that will become the `[[Prototype]]` of all instances created with `new`. `__proto__` is an accessor property (getter/setter on `Object.prototype`) exposing an instance's internal `[[Prototype]]` link. Modern code should always use `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)` and `Object.setPrototypeOf(obj)` instead of `__proto__`.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: The universal test for prototypal inheritance clarity.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is at the very end of the JavaScript prototype chain?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: At the end of every standard prototype chain is `Object.prototype`. The `[[Prototype]]` of `Object.prototype` is strictly `null`. Attempting to look up a property on `null` terminates the prototype walk and returns `undefined`.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Verifies knowledge of the terminal prototype boundary.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why is Object.create(null) useful?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `Object.create(null)` creates a dictionary object with NO prototype (`[[Prototype]] === null`). It has zero inherited properties: no `toString`, no `hasOwnProperty`, no `constructor`. It is safe from prototype pollution attacks and makes a pure key-value hash map.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests security awareness and dictionary object design.

realWorldUseCases.description: Config parsers create `Object.create(null)` containers to ensure malicious payloads containing `__proto__` cannot inject properties into global prototypes.
ORMs walk prototype chains to inspect entity class decorators and metadata across base models.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: let curr = entity.constructor; while (curr && curr !== Object) { inspect(curr); curr = Object.getPrototypeOf(curr); }

howToExplain.opening: JavaScript uses prototypal inheritance where objects have an internal [[Prototype]] link to another object. Property lookups walk this chain upwards until found or until reaching null.
keyPoints: Every object links to a prototype object via its internal [[Prototype]] slot.
Standard objects inherit from Object.prototype, whose prototype is null.
constructor.prototype defines what instances will link to.
Object.getPrototypeOf is the standard accessor; Object.create(null) creates pure dictionary maps.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Unlike classical class-based languages with rigid vtables, JavaScript inheritance is a dynamic linked-list traversal.
analogies: Like asking for help: if you don't know the answer, you ask your manager; if they don't know, they ask their director, until you reach the CEO (Object.prototype), after which there is no one left (null).

commonMistakes.why: __proto__ is a legacy Annex B feature with performance deoptimizations in modern JIT engines.

followUpDeepDive.question: What performance penalty does Object.setPrototypeOf incur in V8?
followUpDeepDive.answer: In V8, mutating an object's prototype via `Object.setPrototypeOf` alters the object's hidden class (Map/Shape) transition tree, immediately invalidating all inline caches (ICs) across the entire codebase that touch that object shape.
